question: stringly_typed
why: This codebase has real examples of both classes, so nothing here is constructed. The positives are deliberate designs, not accidents — a CLI has to accept strings at its edge — which is exactly why the question is worth asking of something that already passes every lint.

items.name: questions
items.why: Two Option<&str> encode 'inline JSON or a path, but not both'. A caller can pass both, or neither, and only find out at runtime.

items.name: text
items.why: The &str is a literal value or the sentinel `-`. The sentinel is a second meaning smuggled into the same type.

items.name: items
items.why: Same sentinel, same smuggling: a path, or `-` meaning stdin.

items.name: code_for
items.why: Returns &'static str drawn from a fixed set of contract codes. An enum would make a typo fail to compile.

items.name: read_only
items.why: The &str is a human-readable title. Any string is genuinely valid.

items.name: add
items.why: Two token counts as u64, where every u64 is a legitimate count.

items.name: retryable
items.why: Takes a typed &Error and returns a genuine yes/no. The bool is the whole answer, not a stand-in for one.

items.name: build_cli
items.why: Takes nothing and returns a built type. No value to mistype.
